reviewer: root original-endpoint review with independent PI audit
reason: The proposed CH enrichment after both anchor sides is also predicted by a shared CH-heavy formula or register. Persistent meaning need not produce literal copying of the written anchor side. The enrichment baseline, weighting, balancing rule and held partition are unspecified. GDT873 uses a different density endpoint and a selected half of eligible anchors; it does not test or falsify this proposal.

design.contrast: anchor-independent common-procedure response versus persistent anchor-side setting
design.countermodel: A position-only or formula-composition effect can create the same CH-side excess without operand classes or a procedure response meaning.
design.falsifier: In a held, independently coded table the response side consistently copies anchor side after the same strata are fixed, or the CH excess vanishes when anchor identity is balanced; the common-procedure account then loses its restricted prediction.
design.mechanism: operand-class anchor followed by a common procedure response class
design.prediction: After fixed direction, lag-band, paragraph and folio strata are declared, CH-side responses should remain enriched after both CH and SH anchors if the response is a common procedure class; a persistent setting predicts response side copying the anchor side.
design.principal_risk: GDT872 is raw co-occurrence only; no anchor, response, operand or procedure meaning is independently bound. This is exploratory and does not add the GDT873 position control.
design.related: Near GDT872 and the persistent-setting/reset family, but the proposed discriminator is anchor-side invariance of a downstream response class, not forward density or a reset.
design.smallest_next_step: Freeze anchor-side, direction, lag-band, paragraph and folio strata; then inspect held response-side records without changing the GDT872 pair inventory.

source_evidence.quote:
The response-side composition is worth preserving separately: in distal within-
paragraph ZL hits,41/51 forward responses are CH-side versus36/66 backward.
Forward CH-side responses occur after both CH anchors (25/31) and SH anchors
(16/20). Thus pooled same-side concordance is misleading as a state-copying
interpretation. The strict diagnostic has7/9 CH-side forward and5/6 backward;
it does not reproduce the primary directional composition contrast. Its small,
selectively retained sample does not prove the primary contrast false either.
All nine response pairs contribute distal hits; the counts are retained rather
than selecting a winning pair after inspection.
